claims.evidence: Microsoft has unveiled a public preview of Windows Server 2028 with a new approach to security by default. As Ars Technica reports , the system will introduce Hardened Server Core, a set of settings that, according to the company, aligns with strengthened U.S. Department of Defense guidelines, including the DISA Security Technical Implementation Guide recommendations. It was already added to Windows Server 2025 in an update, but administrators had to activate the feature manually at the time. The new stack eliminates NVMe translation through SCSI and, according to Microsoft, is expected to reduce overhead and improve performance. The release notes list a known issue with the implementation of TLS hybrid key exchange: if hybrid groups are negotiated by a TLS server, the LSASS service may crash. Until the bug is fixed, Microsoft recommends disabling such key exchange groups. The hardened settings will be available only for Server Core installations. The company urged users to test the build and report which specific settings interfere with applications. Microsoft will also strengthen requirements for authentication through Remote Desktop and PowerShell script block logging. Hardware-supported security mechanisms, including Secure Boot and DMA requirements, will not be applied until a later preview build.
